title: Infra-Low Frequency Neurofeedback
subtitle: Training very slow signal fluctuations
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating infra-low frequency neurofeedback within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain infra-low frequency neurofeedback without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in infra-low frequency neurofeedback.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to infra-low frequency neurofeedback.

sections.explainSimply: ILF protocols use very low-frequency signal components and often rely on clinician-guided frequency adjustment.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Proposed mechanisms and optimal parameters remain debated. Very slow signals are vulnerable to drift, movement, sweat and equipment characteristics.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Transparent reporting of filters, coupling, target frequency and adverse-response management is essential. Controlled clinical evidence remains limited.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand infra-low frequency neurofeedback to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Very slow does not mean deep, specific or automatically safe.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using infra-low frequency neurofeedback predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Very slow does not mean deep, specific or automatically safe. Evidence classification: emerging; insufficient controlled evidence.
